Comprehensive multi-task evaluation with task-appropriate baselines and metrics; solid ablation studies (Table 3) validating design choices (CoCa over CLIP, frozen encoder, model scale, Stage 1 importance)

strengths: Addresses a genuine practical need: B-rep is the industry standard for CAD storage, yet prior work focused on point clouds/images. Using B-rep directly is both principled and practical.
Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse tasks (reverse engineering, completion, error correction, CAD-QA) with appropriate baselines and multiple metrics.

Strong empirical results: 48.7% CD improvement vs. CADCL in reverse engineering (0.009 IR), substantial gains in completion and error correction, competitive performance on CAD-QA with significantly smaller model (1.5B vs 7B parameters).

Sound technical design: CoCa-based alignment justifiably chosen for capturing both global and fine-grained features; two-stage training strategy (reverse engineering pre-training → downstream adaptation) is conceptually well-motivated.

Honest analysis of limitations: Thoughtful discussion of modeling ambiguity (Fig. 5) explaining why different valid sequences generate identical geometry—scientifically responsible acknowledgment rather than dismissal.
Proper ablation studies (Table 3) justifying design choices: CoCa vs. CLIP, encoder freezing, model size, projector depth, and Stage 1 importance.
Clear presentation with effective visualizations; framework and methodology are easy to follow and reproduce.
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Each core component is borrowed (UV-Net encoding from [13], Python-like code from [19], CoCa alignment from [42], standard two-stage training). The main contribution is integration/engineering rather than novel methods. Loss weights (λ_con=1, λ_cap=2) copied from CoCa without CAD-domain tuning.

Narrow evaluation scope: Single-source dataset (DeepCAD only, 170K sequences) with no cross-dataset generalization testing to other CAD systems. Small CAD-QA dataset (1K models). No real-world industrial CAD evaluation or zero-shot assessment.

Fairness concerns in comparisons: Error correction compares B-rep input to 2D image-based commercial models (asymmetric modalities); Completion uses text descriptions for CAD-Llama vs. B-rep for BrepCoder; ReCAD comparison uses different datasets (OpenSCAD vs. DeepCAD).

Modest improvements from Stage 1 pre-training: Completion shows only +0.43% ACC_cmd and +0.03% ACC_param gains; error correction shows mixed results. Only CAD-QA shows substantial +8% improvement, questioning Stage 1 necessity for other tasks.

Insufficient failure analysis: No discussion of causes for 0.9% Invalid Ratio or which CAD design types fail. Limited explanation of why ACC_cmd (89.39%) lags CADCL (90.31%) beyond modeling ambiguity examples. No qualitative failure cases shown.

Inadequate scalability investigation: Model size tested only at 1.5B and 0.5B; computational costs of two-stage training vs. end-to-end fine-tuning not analyzed; performance degradation with model complexity unexplored; practical deployment considerations absent.

Under-justified design choices: Encoder freezing yields only 2.8% improvement over unfrozen (0.516 vs 0.499 CD); statistical significance unclear. Projector architecture (3 MLP+GELU) appears arbitrary without ablation. LLM backbone sensitivity (why Qwen 2.5-1.5B?) not explored.
CAD-QA performance is competitive but not state-of-the-art: 79% vs 81% for PointLLM, which with 4-choice QA means absolute gains are marginal.

Missing comparisons: No evaluation against other CAD MLLMs (CAD-MLLM [38], CADGPT [34]) on shared tasks. BrepLLM not compared (though paper justifies this). Limited discussion of task-specific SOTA comparison.

Reproducibility gaps: No mention of code/data availability. Hyperparameter choices (256 queries, hidden dimension 512) unjustified. Data augmentation for error correction/completion tasks poorly documented ('50%-80% ratio' unclear).

Honest treatment of limitations: acknowledges modeling ambiguity (Figure 5) with statistical evidence, showing 14.14% of low-CD results have low ACC_cmd
